name: Rich Harrison
notes: Go-go/breakbeat R&B, and the research calls it "the most percussion-dense board in the lane", 1999–2006. The band is "90–115 straight (backbeat 2&4, with the go-go feel accenting across all 16ths)", mode 100. This is a producer model, so the board deltas are authored hardest and they are the loudest in the section: he "flips a **short drum-and-guitar breakdown** and adds hand percussion — bongo, cowbell and ride cymbal", producing "'cascading drums', near-continuous 16th/32nd activity, second-line and go-go accent patterns, **no quantised hat lane**". So the kick runs four to eight hits a bar with the secondary anchor on `1a` and a 0.34 offbeat-8th share, the snare carries ghosts across six 16th off-slots at a 0.66 probability, the hat is explicitly non-continuous but at 0.9 fill density with a 32nd/64th roll vocabulary at 0.8 per bar and open hats on all four offbeats, the perc bed is five lanes at six to ten hits a bar sitting only 1 dB under the kit, `quantizeStrength` is 0.52 and fills come every two bars. Harmony is the sourced relationship, and it is unusual enough that the entry states it in words: "D minor with the sampled material sitting on B♭ and G — **'two major chords a minor third apart'**" — that is `VI` and `IV` over a minor tonic, and `VI–IV` is the top-weighted family here. "He plays all the instrumental parts himself and works extremely fast", with horn samples as the hook — the counter at −12 with `answer_lick` leading. "No 808 — the source break's bass and guitar carry the low-mid; he resists adding instruments" is why there is no `bass808` block and the bass walks at a 0.56 root follow. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every velocity, density and jitter number; the research sources the sample lineage, key relationships, tempo, instrumentation and working speed, not a velocity map. ⚠ `session.keys` is part-sourced: the entry names `Dm`, and the remaining values `Gm`, `Am`, `Cm`, together with all 4 weights, are INFERRED rather than read from the entry. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry's harmony line is "D minor with the sampled material sitting on B-flat and G - "two major chords a minor third apart" (i.e. `VI` and `IV` over a minor tonic)", and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern") — so a `vamp`-dominant weighting rendered a **one**-chord bed the research nowhere describes. The entry names both chords, so the family has to reach its second one: `2_bars_per_chord` now carries it, with `vamp` as the minority. `1_per_bar` is not authored — a sample-led loop moves at the sample's rate, and the entry gives no faster one.
